policy: SCI-1 candidate evidence and relationships, drafted by the AI agent and all pending. Not read by the decision engine or the app: nothing here is scored or displayed until a named human reviewer approves it and a separate change (SCI-2) moves it into the scenario. A verified quote is not a scientific approval.

evidence.quote: In the absence of strong evidence for sedimentary structures, the Margin unit could alternatively be a pyroclastic or extrusive or intrusive igneous deposit.
evidence.summary: The missing sedimentary structures are what keeps an igneous origin of the Margin unit possible (Margin-unit-wide statement; the same words appear in the Lefroy Bay report).

evidence.quote: the absence of distinctive sedimentary structures leaves open the possibility that this rock is igneous (and altered).
evidence.summary: For Pelican Point, the absence of distinctive sedimentary structures is the stated reason the igneous alternative stays open.

evidence.quote: The western Margin lacks clear sedimentary structures at the outcrop level, including at Bunsen Peak.
evidence.summary: Outcrop-scale observation for the western Margin: no clear sedimentary structures.

evidence.quote: This appearance is distinctly different from the eastern Margin from which the Pelican Point and Lefroy Bay samples were collected, where mostly tabular or plate-like outcrop occurs in a relatively flat landscape.
evidence.summary: The eastern Margin (Pelican Point, Lefroy Bay) and the western Margin (Comet Geyser) look distinctly different at outcrop scale.

evidence.quote: Although the elevation of Comet Geyser is 25 meters higher than Lefroy Bay, their relative position within any Margin stratigraphy has not been established.
evidence.summary: The relative stratigraphic position of the sampled Margin sites is not established.

evidence.quote: In the absence of readily interpreted sedimentary structures, if the Margin unit is sedimentary, it may have been deposited in almost any setting: shoreline, fluviolacustrine, aeolian or pyroclastic.
evidence.summary: Without readable sedimentary structures, even a sedimentary Margin unit cannot be tied to a setting (shoreline, river/lake, wind, pyroclastic).

evidence.quote: The Hans Amundsen Memorial Workspace is a dusty, light-toned, granular, fractured and minimally layered in-place outcrop.
evidence.summary: Natural Margin surfaces can be dusty and only minimally layered, a limit for stand-off reading of structures.

evidence.quote: SuperCam analyses indicate that the rocks in the vicinity of Bunsen Peak are compositionally heterogeneous, and similar to previous measurements of the Margin unit.
evidence.summary: Stand-off chemistry already shows heterogeneity near Bunsen Peak, similar to earlier Margin measurements.

evidence.quote: It can identify the chemical and mineral makeup of areas on Mars as small as a pencil point, from a distance of more than 20 feet (7 meters).
evidence.summary: NASA's description of SuperCam: stand-off chemical and mineral makeup of small spots.

evidence.quote: Mastcam-Z has cameras that can zoom in, focus, and take 3D pictures and video at high speed to allow detailed examination of distant objects.
evidence.summary: NASA's description of Mastcam-Z: zoom and 3D imaging of distant objects (outcrop structure).

evidence.quote: The Amherst Point abrasion reveals a moderately to poorly sorted medium to coarse-grained, aqueously altered rock tentatively identified as a sandstone, with a cement likely composed of silica.
evidence.summary: What the first Margin abrasion showed (Pelican Point): a tentatively identified, silica-cemented sandstone.

evidence.quote: The rock texture is consistent with a moderately to poorly sorted coarse sandstone or an altered igneous rock.
evidence.summary: For Comet Geyser, the abraded texture did not decide between sandstone and altered igneous rock.

evidence.quote: Mineralogy and chemistry are consistent with a sandstone (possibly at least partially altered in-situ), or a heavily altered igneous rock, e.g. a listvenite.
evidence.summary: For Comet Geyser, in-situ mineralogy and chemistry did not decide between the two either; in-situ alteration is stated as compatible with both host rocks.

evidence.quote: Comet Geyser appears more enriched in alteration materials than either of the other Margin unit samples.
evidence.summary: The three Margin samples differ: Comet Geyser is the most altered.

evidence.quote: Here the landscape consists of resistant dark-toned high-standing and often massive outcrop interbedded with lighter-toned low-lying rocks.
evidence.summary: The western Margin has two rock expressions: dark-toned high-standing outcrop and lighter-toned low-lying rocks (which one was sampled: ev-cg-bunsen-high-standing).

evidence.quote: The Bunsen Peak workspace consists of a high-standing, resistant, dark-toned and smooth rock which stands ~ 1 m above lighter-toned low-lying rocks.
evidence.summary: The Bunsen Peak workspace, where Comet Geyser was cored and Castle Geyser abraded, is the dark-toned, high-standing rock, about 1 m above the lighter-toned low-lying rocks.

evidence.quote: It is not certain that Bunsen Peak is in-place, but similarities with surrounding bedrock strongly support a genetic relationship with them.
evidence.summary: Whether the sampled Bunsen Peak rock is in place is uncertain; the report judges it genetically related to the surrounding bedrock.

evidence.quote: It identifies chemical elements at a tiny scale.
evidence.summary: NASA's description of PIXL (X-ray spectrometer): fine-scale elemental chemistry.

evidence.quote: SHERLOC is assisted by WATSON, a color camera for taking close-up images of rock grains and surface textures.
evidence.summary: NASA's description of WATSON with SHERLOC: close-up images of grains and textures.

evidence.quote: SHERLOC uses cameras, spectrometers, and a laser to search for organics and minerals that have been altered by watery environments
evidence.summary: NASA's description of SHERLOC: organics and water-altered minerals.

evidence.quote: Detailed laboratory study of the suite of grains/clasts would address this unknown
evidence.summary: Laboratory study would address whether the carbonate is detrital or formed in situ. Source: Comet Geyser initial report (M2020-1088-27), Returned Sample Science Considerations. The scenario and registry locators for this quote said "Pelican Point initial report" until they were corrected on 2026-11-07.

evidence.quote: the origin of the carbonate, whether detrital grains or the result of in situ alteration, is still unknown.
evidence.summary: The open question the laboratory study would address (Comet Geyser report).

evidence.quote: pervasive water/rock interaction leading to extensive mineral carbonation likely in a subsurface environment.
evidence.summary: The report frames the returned Comet Geyser sample as testing either a source-to-sink sedimentary system or pervasive subsurface mineral carbonation.

evidence.quote: analyses of the three Margin unit samples could document details of their igneous origin (provided adequately unaltered material remains).
evidence.summary: If the Margin unit is igneous, the three existing Margin samples could already serve the laboratory question (conditional).

evidence.quote: Comet Geyser is the third sample of the Margin campaign
evidence.summary: Three Margin samples exist (Pelican Point, Lefroy Bay, Comet Geyser).

evidence.quote: Crystallization ages of detrital igneous clasts and/or minerals within the Pelican Point sample would provide upper bounds on the timing of deposition of the Margin unit.
evidence.summary: A laboratory question an existing Margin core is already proposed for (conditional on return).

evidence.quote: Mars Sample Return (MSR) was a proposed multi-mission campaign by NASA and ESA (European Space Agency) to bring carefully selected samples from Mars to Earth.
evidence.summary: As retrieved on 2026-11-07, NASA's Mars Sample Return page describes MSR in the past tense, as a proposed campaign. No other status claim is made here.

proposals.reasoning: The PDS reports name the presence or absence of sedimentary structures as what keeps the sedimentary and igneous origins apart. A stand-off survey that images outcrop structure (Mastcam-Z zoom and 3D) at outcrops not yet examined bears directly on that question.
limitations: Absence of structures does not favour either origin; only their presence would (ev-pp-no-structures-sample).
The western Margin already lacks clear structures at outcrop level (ev-cg-west-no-structures); whether other outcrops show them is unknown.
Dusty, minimally layered surfaces may hide structures (ev-pp-dusty-outcrop).
No source places a suitable outcrop at Target A.
proposals.affectsComparison: Hypothetical future result, not a current one: only if a reviewer approves this link and SCI-2 later adopts it into the scored data would Survey be linked to 2 of 3 open questions (2025-05-06); today it is linked to 1 of 3. No score is computed here.

proposals.reasoning: The rover-based Pelican Point interpretation (silica-cemented sandstone) is evidence for the unit-level sedimentary hypothesis. Linking it would let evidence quality see the existing rover data instead of reporting only orbital support.
limitations: New relationship type: the current schema links observations to interpretations, not sample interpretations to unit hypotheses (data-model change, SCI-2).
The interpretation is tentative and preliminary.
proposals.affectsComparison: Evidence quality would no longer be identical for the three actions on this question (SCI-2 decides how).

proposals.reasoning: The Comet Geyser report raises an altered intrusive igneous origin, and says the same could apply to the two earlier Margin samples; that is rover-based evidence bearing on the crystalline-igneous hypothesis.
limitations: Same schema limitation as above.
The report leaves the question undetermined; this is support for considering the hypothesis, not for preferring it.
proposals.affectsComparison: As above: evidence quality would reflect existing rover data.

proposals.reasoning: Outcome A: distinctive sedimentary structures observed at outcrop scale → favours hyp-sedimentary and weakens hyp-crystalline-igneous. Outcome B: no structures observed → favours none (the reports say absence leaves both open).
limitations: Pyroclastic deposits can also be layered; outcome A may not separate sedimentary from pyroclastic.
Draft only; the engine scores nothing from it until approved and moved into the scenario (SCI-2).
proposals.affectsComparison: Would make hypothesis discrimination evaluable for Survey (SCI-2).

proposals.reasoning: No outcome is source-supported yet: for Comet Geyser, abraded texture and in-situ chemistry were each stated as consistent with both a sandstone and an altered igneous rock. A discriminating outcome would need a lithology not yet abraded or a texture the three abrasions did not show; the sources do not specify one. The lighter-toned low-lying western Margin rocks are a source-named rock expression that the Comet Geyser sample did not come from; whether they were abraded later, and what they are, is not established here.
limitations: This records the absence of a source-supported discriminating outcome. It is not evidence that abrasion has no scientific value.
proposals.affectsComparison: Hypothesis discrimination for Abrade stays unsupported until a reviewer defines a discriminating outcome.

proposals.reasoning: Conditional on return to Earth. The laboratory test is about how the carbonate formed, which is not the same question as the host rock's origin. Detrital carbonate grains → favours hyp-sedimentary (the source's source-to-sink framing). Carbonate formed in situ → informs the alteration process (e.g. mineral carbonation) but does not by itself favour either host-rock hypothesis: in-situ alteration is stated as compatible with a sandstone as well as an altered igneous rock (ev-cg-chemistry-either).
limitations: Conditional on sample return, which NASA's page now describes in the past tense (ev-nasa-msr-status).
Three Margin cores already exist and are proposed for the same laboratory questions (ev-cg-three-samples-igneous, ev-pp-geochronology); the added value of a further core is not established.
Extends the existing pending assessment da-core-detrital-carbonate (adds the in-situ outcome and its condition).
proposals.affectsComparison: Would make hypothesis discrimination evaluable for Core, with an explicit condition (SCI-2).
